_description: Scenario grid multipliers. Each trade activates at most one base market-state weighting (first match in priority order). Zero or more PM preference overlays are then applied on top. The combined multipliers are converted to normalized weights for weighted-average structure evaluation.
_selection: Base weightings are evaluated top-to-bottom and the first full match is applied. PM overlays are evaluated independently and all matching overlays stack on top of the base grid. Order matters for base weightings, but not for overlays.
_what_the_weights_mean: Each multiplier scales the importance of one explicit grid cell. A value of 1.0 means baseline importance; higher values emphasize the scenario, lower values de-emphasize it. Final structure scoring uses a weighted average across valid cells.
_baseline_logic: All valid grid cells start at the universal baseline multiplier. The active base weighting overrides individual cells. Matching PM overlays then multiply specific cells on top. Final scenario weights are the normalized multipliers over the valid cells for that tenor.

scenario_column_descriptions.S: No move — spot ends unchanged from today (the grid's spot-anchored centre). Tests time decay and vol sensitivity in isolation. The forward is shown per time-row as a decaying reference.
scenario_column_descriptions.t%→K: Early touch then retrace — spot trades through the target at this time point but mean-reverts before expiry. Critical for path-dependent features: barriers, American-style triggers, and structures whose value is locked in on a touch.
scenario_column_descriptions.K−½σ: Falls just short — spot ends half a sigma short of the target, in the direction of the view. A partial move that does not quite reach the objective; tests whether the structure still pays when the move undershoots the target.
scenario_column_descriptions.K: Target hit — spot ends at the target level. The PM's directional view plays out as expected.
scenario_column_descriptions.K+½σ: Overshoot — spot moves significantly beyond the target. Tests whether the structure captures or is exposed to extended moves beyond the initial objective.
scenario_column_descriptions.−½σ: Modest adverse move — spot drifts half a sigma against the trade. A mild correction or slow bleed; tests whether the structure bleeds slowly or holds up on a partial reversal.
scenario_column_descriptions.−1σ: Full reversal — spot moves a full sigma against the trade. A significant adverse outcome; tests maximum loss and whether the structure has asymmetric downside.
scenario_column_descriptions.Δvol: Vol shift — flat directional path but implied vol moves. Isolates vega exposure independently of direction; most relevant for structures with significant optionality or vega asymmetry.

driver_glossary.Carry: Decay / roll-down — value from the forward grinding toward (or against) spot at unchanged spot (the 'no move' cell). Positive when the carry works for the view.
driver_glossary.Directional: Directional capture — value as spot progresses toward, reaches, or overshoots the target.
driver_glossary.Adverse: Adverse moves — P&L when spot moves the wrong way (half / full sigma against the view).
driver_glossary.Vega: Vol shock — P&L from a vol move at unchanged spot (isolated vega).

base_weightings.comment: Baseline carry trade: carry-to-vol H or M, moderate target distance, with carry. PM preferences are handled separately as overlays.

commentary.market_behavior: Spot is sticky or slow-moving toward the target; the forward roll-down dominates and vol is not a main driver, though adverse moves can still happen. Overshoot is rare; undershoot is more likely.
commentary.trade_guidance: Privilege trades that are decay-resistant, benefit from the carry, and accrue most of their value later in the life — low delta at the onset.

base_weightings.comment: Large expected move (>1.25σ from forward), any carry, any direction. PM style overlays can further tilt this, but the base market state is simply that the trade is positioned for a meaningful displacement.

commentary.market_behavior: Positioned for a large, decisive displacement (>1.25σ from the forward). Reaching the target needs a sustained, conviction-driven move, and when these happen they often overshoot. The path matters less than reaching or exceeding the target.
commentary.trade_guidance: Privilege trades with strong directional capture (high delta to the move) and upside if spot overshoots the target; cheap decay-resistance matters less than payoff on the move itself.

base_weightings.comment: Tenor under 1 month: theta and pin risk dominate everything else. The terminal intrinsic value (EXPIRY) is what the PM should focus on — there is almost no time for path scenarios to develop independently from the final outcome. Early-touch scenarios are near-equivalent to expiry at this horizon and should be de-emphasised to avoid double-counting.

commentary.market_behavior: Short tenor (<1 month) — theta and pin risk dominate; there is little time for path scenarios to develop independently of the final outcome, so terminal intrinsic value is what matters.
commentary.trade_guidance: Privilege trades whose value is the terminal payoff at the target with low time-decay drag; path-dependent and slow-accrual structures have little room to work.

base_weightings.comment: High carry (regime 2) trading against the carry: the carry is a structural, continuous headwind. Every day the trade is open, theta and the forward drift both work against the position. The dominant risk is an adverse drift (WRONG_WAY) and a flat market that bleeds premium (NO_MOVE). Getting to the target requires the market to fight its own structural tendency — CORRECT_PATH is the hardest outcome to achieve.

commentary.market_behavior: Trading against a strong carry — theta and the forward drift are a continuous headwind every day the trade is open. The dominant risks are an adverse drift and a flat market that bleeds premium; reaching the target means fighting the market's structural tendency.
commentary.trade_guidance: Privilege trades that limit bleed and stay robust to a slow adverse drift; cheap, decay-light structures with a defined cost are favoured over carry-dependent ones.

base_weightings.comment: High carry, trading with the carry, targeting a distant level (>1.5σ from forward). The drift is your ally and the target requires a sustained, conviction-driven move. When these moves happen they often overshoot. The dominant paths are a smooth carry-driven advance (CORRECT_PATH) and an extension beyond the target (OVERSHOOT). Wrong-way moves are fighting both the drift and the market's natural tendency.

High carry, trading with the carry, targeting a level close to the forward (<0.5σ). This is essentially a carry-capture trade — the target is so close that normal market noise will touch it. The main risk is an early touch followed by a reversal before expiry (EARLY_TARGET). A sustained correct-path move is also likely. Overshoot is less meaningful at this distance.

High carry, trading with the carry, moderate target distance. The drift is working in our favour. A smooth progression toward the target is the most likely path. Wrong-way moves require the market to work against both the direction of the trade and the carry, which is a double headwind for the adverse scenario.

Noisy carry (regime 0) with elevated vol (>20%): there is no reliable directional drift signal, and vol moves are large enough to materially affect option value independent of direction. The dominant driver of P&L is the vol surface, not the forward path. VOL_SENSITIVITY scenarios deserve heavy weight. A flat market (NO_MOVE) is less meaningful without carry pressure.

Noisy carry (regime 0): the carry signal is weak relative to vol. The trade is a pure directional bet without a structural drift to support it. Vol-driven mean reversion is a larger factor than in high-carry regimes. NO_MOVE is less meaningful (there is no carry bleed), and VOL_SENSITIVITY deserves more weight.

commentary.market_behavior: A pure directional bet with no structural drift to lean on; the carry signal is weak relative to vol, so vol-driven mean reversion matters more and a flat market does not bleed via carry. No-move is less meaningful here.
commentary.trade_guidance: Privilege clean directional exposure to the target with manageable vega; carry-capture structures add little because there is no carry to harvest.

base_weightings.comment: Tenor over 6 months: there is a large window for the market to reach the target early and then drift away before expiry — a real risk for capped structures and spreads. EARLY_TARGET (touch-and-retrace) deserves elevated weight. Vol sensitivity also matters more because vol moves have more time to compound.

commentary.market_behavior: Long tenor (>6 months) — a large window for spot to reach the target early and then drift away before expiry, and for vol moves to compound. Early-touch-then-retrace is a real risk, especially for capped structures.
commentary.trade_guidance: Privilege trades that lock in value on the path or hold up if the target is reached early and then given back; beware capped structures that only pay at expiry.

base_weightings.comment: Target is distant from the forward (>1.5σ) with moderate carry. Getting there requires a sustained move with conviction — which tends to overshoot. Early touches are unlikely at this distance. This applies when carry is not the dominant factor (carry_regime 0 or 1) so the signal is purely about the target distance.

Target is close to the forward (<0.5σ) with moderate carry. The level is so easy to reach that random noise will touch it. The dominant risk for capped structures is an early touch followed by a pull-back — the trade gets triggered but then reverses. Overshooting a level this close is less informative.

ATM vol above 20% with moderate carry (regime 1). Large vol moves are a meaningful source of P&L variation beyond directional outcomes. Vega-rich structures benefit; short-vol structures are exposed. Elevate VOL_SENSITIVITY to reflect this.

preference_overlays.comment: Cost-focused PM overlay. Penalise scenarios where premium decays without payout, especially slow-bleed or flat paths.
Risk-clean PM overlay. Penalise ugly tail or overshoot outcomes where a structure can leave a messy mark-to-market.
Early-monetisation PM overlay. Favour scenarios where mark-to-market responds faster early in the trade life.
Defendable mark-to-market PM overlay. Tilt away from noisy or extreme paths and toward smoother, easier-to-defend outcomes.
